deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is a draft of the existence part of Riemann's 'Dirichlet principle' argument, in the form it takes in his Inauguraldissertation (1851, §§16–18). The previous page discusses the worry that the infimum might only be approached by discontinuous functions, and the outline of the 'three parts' of the essay.

Setup (lines 1–9). T is a (possibly multiply connected) surface. α and β are real, single-valued functions of (x,y) on T. Define
  Ω(α) = ∫_T [ (α_x − β_y)^2 + (α_y + β_x)^2 ] dT.
α may not have arbitrary discontinuities, since these would make Ω infinite. The admissible class is all α with the same prescribed boundary values on ∂T. For these, Ω is finite and by its nature never negative.

Riemann then concludes (this is the unjustified step) that for at least one function u the integral attains a minimum value. In local terms: every α infinitely little different from u gives Ω(α) > Ω(u).

Variation. Let σ be an arbitrary continuous function of position on T, vanishing everywhere on the boundary, and h a constant. (Crossed-out intermediate: Ω(u+hσ) = Ω(u) + 2Mh + Nh^2.) Expanding the square:
  Ω(u+hσ) = Ω(u) + 2h ∫ [ (u_x − β_y) σ_x + (u_y + β_x) σ_y ] dT + h^2 ∫ (σ_x^2 + σ_y^2) dT.
If u is a minimum, Ω(u+hσ) − Ω(u) must be ≥ 0 for small h of both signs. Hence the linear coefficient M must vanish (the crossed-out text says exactly this, about the coefficient of h). Then
  Ω(u+hσ) = Ω(u) + h^2 ∫ (σ_x^2 + σ_y^2) dT.

Uniqueness. Suppose u+σ were also a minimum.
- If Ω(u+σ) > Ω(u): then for 0<h<1, Ω(u+hσ) = Ω(u) + h^2 N < Ω(u) + N = Ω(u+σ). So points arbitrarily close to u+σ (h→1⁻) have smaller value, and u+σ is not a minimum.
- If Ω(u+σ) = Ω(u): then N = ∫|∇σ|^2 = 0. So σ is constant, and since σ=0 on the boundary, σ ≡ 0.
Hence Ω has a minimum for one function u only.

First variation / Euler–Lagrange. For the unique minimizer u, the term proportional to h vanishes for every admissible σ:
  2h ∫ dT [ (u_x − β_y) σ_x + (u_y + β_x) σ_y ] = 0.
From this Riemann infers two things:
- the functions X = u_x − β_y and Y = u_y + β_x are not discontinuous along a line (a weak-form regularity remark);
- they satisfy ∂X/∂x + ∂Y/∂y = 0. My addition: integrate by parts using σ|∂T = 0; the page omits '= 0'.
For smooth β this is just Δu = 0, since −β_yx + β_xy = 0.

The crossed-out last lines start the next step, as in the dissertation: X dy − Y dx is a complete differential. Integrating it, after cutting a multiply connected T by cross-cuts (Querschnitte) into a simply connected one, gives a function ν with ν_y = X and ν_x = −Y. Setting v = ν + β gives u_x = v_y and u_y = −v_x. So u + iv is an analytic function whose imaginary part differs from β by a regular function; this is the theme of the previous page's W = u + (β − V)i.
errors: Existence of the minimum is asserted from 'Ω is finite and nonnegative, so some function gives a minimum'. This is invalid: a nonnegative functional has an infimum, but it need not be attained in the admissible class. This is the gap later criticised by Weierstrass (1870); Riemann's own previous page voices this exact worry, then the draft proceeds anyway.

The formula Ω(u+hσ) = Ω(u) + h^2∫|∇σ|^2 is written before the vanishing of the linear term is formally stated. The order of exposition is loose (it relies on the crossed-out argument), but there is no logical error once the linear term is zero.

Passing from the weak equation ∫(Xσ_x + Yσ_y) = 0 to the pointwise PDE ∂X/∂x + ∂Y/∂y = 0 needs regularity of u (or Weyl's lemma). Riemann only adds 'nicht längs einer Linie unstetig', which is not a proof.
The 'minimum' is defined only locally (against functions infinitely little different from u). The uniqueness argument nonetheless works, because of the exact quadratic structure (convexity) of Ω.
Minor: the final displayed equation on the page lacks '= 0'.

results.what: Minimization of the Dirichlet-type functional Ω(α)=∫((α_x−β_y)^2+(α_y+β_x)^2)dT over α with prescribed boundary values, with existence of a minimizer assumed from Ω ≥ 0
results.modern_name: Dirichlet principle (variational existence of harmonic / analytic functions)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (1839), W. Thomson (1847), Dirichlet (lectures); named and used by Riemann 1851/1857; justified by Hilbert 1900

results.what: Exact second-order expansion Ω(u+hσ)=Ω(u)+2hM+h^2∫|∇σ|^2 and uniqueness of the minimizer via convexity, with σ=const=0 from vanishing Dirichlet energy
results.modern_name: Uniqueness of minimizer of a strictly convex quadratic functional / uniqueness for the Dirichlet problem

results.what: First variation gives the weak equation ∫((u_x−β_y)σ_x+(u_y+β_x)σ_y)dT=0, hence ∂(u_x−β_y)/∂x+∂(u_y+β_x)/∂y=0 and an analytic function u+iv via a conjugate after cross-cuts
results.modern_name: Euler–Lagrange equation (weak form) / construction of the harmonic conjugate on a cut Riemann surface

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of the well-known Dirichlet-principle argument of Riemann's 1851 dissertation (§§16–18), with the same functional Ω, the same h-variation and the same uniqueness argument. It also reused in the 1857 Abelian functions paper. The draft shows Riemann aware of the attainment problem (previous page) yet asserting the minimum, which is a mildly interesting historical detail but already discussed in the literature.

checkable.asserts: Pointwise integrand identity behind Ω(u+hσ)=Ω(u)+2hM+h^2∫(σ_x^2+σ_y^2); the result should be 0
For smooth β, the Euler–Lagrange equation reduces to Laplace's equation Δu=0 (the result should be 0)
For harmonic u and a test function σ vanishing on the boundary of the unit square, the first variation is 0
Ω(u+σ)−Ω(u+hσ)=N(1−h^2)>0 for 0<h<1 when N>0, so u+σ cannot be a minimum

transcription_corrections: Line 'stetige 𝔉 des Orts': the symbol is the abbreviation for 'Function'. The intended reading is roughly 'Bezeichnet man durch σ eine beliebige stetige Function des Orts in der Fläche T, die an der Grenze allenthalben = 0 ist, und durch h eine von x, y unabhängige Größe (Constante)'.
'die an der Grenze von T denselben Werth, dieser annehmen' is better read as 'die an der Grenze von T dieselben Werthe annehmen', i.e. prescribed boundary values.
'die Function α läßt keine beliebige Unstetigkeiten zu, [weil] das Integral dadurch unendlich wird': the connective is causal ('da/weil'), not 'wenn'.
The final displayed equation should end with '= 0', i.e. ∂(u_x−β_y)/∂x + ∂(u_y+β_x)/∂y = 0.
Mid-page 'Ist aber Ω(u+σ)=Ω(u), so muß σ verschwinden' likely reads 'so muß ∫(σ_x^2+σ_y^2)dT verschwinden, also σ constant, und da es in der Begrenzung 0 ist, überall 0 sein'.
